checklist.requirement: Parse with duplicate-key detection, UTF-8/surrogate validation, integer token checks, depth/size bounds and NFC validation; pass JCS vectors with UTF-16 member sorting.
checklist.remaining: Run every positive/negative vector through Android, independent Python and the isolated relay.

checklist.requirement: Derive the deterministic chain identity/admin/recovery keys exactly; validate BIP39 checksum/passphrase behavior. Generate device keys and independent epoch secrets randomly.
checklist.remaining: Connect passphrase input to every root workflow and complete three-party key vectors.

checklist.requirement: Use vetted Ed25519/X25519/HKDF/AEAD/HPKE implementations; reject non-canonical signatures and invalid DH output. Run Appendix C vectors in CI; reference-only HChaCha/HPKE calculations are not production crypto.
checklist.remaining: Complete every Appendix C cryptographic vector and independent negative interoperability case.

checklist.requirement: Enforce secure storage and no persisted mnemonic/root material. Exclude key blobs from portable OS backups; zeroize transient root/session material.
checklist.remaining: Remove remaining normal-key String adapters; test real UI/background/backup/recovery authentication boundaries.

checklist.requirement: Implement exact signed member sets, nested signature coverage, nullable fields, AAD, collection HMAC, frame/buckets, nonce uniqueness and one collection per record.
checklist.remaining: Exercise the complete signed model catalogue, all optional/null cases and size boundaries across three parties.

checklist.requirement: Bind token aud/method/raw path/canonical query/raw body, use 120-second TTL, fresh retry nonce, durable atomic replay protection and ±60-second checks.
checklist.remaining: Execute token freshness/replay/restart/clock uncertainty for every authorization role and retry path.

checklist.requirement: Require approved enrollment/SAS, pending-key acknowledgement, immutable device identities, atomic revocation+rotation, historical authority verification and strict self-healing.
checklist.remaining: Approver UI exports a bounded full public history prefix (signed initial parameters plus every contiguous signed log entry and receipt), polls/binds one request, requires explicit SAS confirmation, transfers the signed certificate and policy-eligible same-generation envelopes, native-verifies the returning DeviceRecord/envelopes, and submits approval. After acceptance it verifies and exports the latest local history together with the signed acceptance receipts; the subject proves that this full history extends the originally selected cut, that each acceptance receipt matches the exact submitted object, stores verified public/ciphertext rows, reads back its envelope and commitment, acknowledges keys, and enters activation. Before offer export, polling, SAS confirmation, and approval, the approver now refreshes the signed log; if the authority head changed since the offer, it fails closed and requires a new ceremony. Exact submitted approvals remain retryable after an uncertain network outcome. Peer approval files use bounded reads, strict UTF-8 decoding, bounded writes and readback; tests cover the exact byte ceiling, first excess byte, malformed UTF-8 and malformed UTF-16 input. The subject's initial and final selected-history files still fail closed on missing prefix evidence or when they exceed their separate current 3.5 MB limit. Kotlin/JNI/AVD ceremony boundary tests pass; isolated-relay approval/readback/ack and concurrent log changes during approval are not yet exercised. Atomic fresh-key enrollment/revocation and independent interop remain untested/incomplete; keep pending. Transfer files contain protocol signed objects and ciphertext; no unspecified file encryption wrapper is added.

checklist.requirement: Enforce complete recovery/device envelope bundles, commitment checks, epoch CAS/hash ancestry, pinned checkpoint rollback/fork checks and mnemonic participation for each new recovery envelope.
checklist.remaining: Mnemonic and peer approver enrollment now create device envelopes for every epoch eligible under the signed retain/windowed/immediate policy and retain only keys for those submitted envelopes (§10.4, §13.5); Rust tests cover multiple eligible epochs and reject a missing current, unordered or duplicate set. Windowed expiry is postponed and post-rotation immediate enrollment is blocked until the local handoff proof passes: the current-generation snapshot must match the verified and materialized log head/hash, have no pending outbox/quarantine/author gaps, have every part receipt durably accepted after inclusion verification, and have its authority-verified compaction in the verified log. Peer subjects validate the policy-minimal epoch set produced after the approver's local proof. Historical epoch-secret removal is guarded by this proof; removed keys get durable expired markers and cannot be retained/read back again. Targeted Robolectric tests verify fail-closed immediate enrollment and windowed expiry when proof is absent; Kotlin compile, ktlint, and detekt pass. Positive proof, actual OS-keystore deletion/readback, all-revoked fresh-subject recovery, enrollment ceremony interoperability, epoch journal/process-death/CAS boundaries against isolated relay and on-device remain incomplete. Full IT-15/16 and independent interoperability remain pending.

checklist.requirement: Implement K/rank/clear/tombstones/history order/policy registers and exact replay deduplication; use binary database collation and safe integers. Preserve conflict evidence in snapshots.
checklist.remaining: Complete every conflict example independently, snapshot preservation and concurrent reorder/UI evidence.

checklist.requirement: Keep default histories without automatic deletion, enforce safety ceilings as bounded projections, use disk/cold indexes and 100–500-row keyset UI pages, display partial progress/capacity state.
checklist.remaining: Settings and device-history screens display distinct downloaded/verified/materialized positions, separate transparency checkpoint/target, pending outbox/author gaps/quarantine, and logical history counts against safety ceilings. The settings label now correctly names its first position as downloaded rather than conflating it with a remote target; status progression/partial-state tests cover D/V/M and transparency separately. Kotlin/JVM 490/490, Android instrumentation 27/27, detekt, ktlint, and Kotlin compile pass. Run real-size Android history stress at safety ceilings and record memory/disk/first-page results; keep pending.

checklist.requirement: Use durable transactional outbox/apply/cursor state, distinguish downloaded/verified/materialized marks, and preserve errors/quarantine evidence across restart.
checklist.remaining: Inject every persistence/cursor boundary with actual restart, capacity failure and uncertain network outcome.

checklist.requirement: Verify full snapshot state and trusted source before bootstrap/pruning; retain cold history, tombstones, boundaries, identity hashes, registry/epoch history and author evidence.
checklist.remaining: The incoming snapshot verifier streams each signature- and AEAD-authenticated plaintext part into a separate Room staging journal; JCS entries are retained atomically with exact part identity. Plaintext entry queries remain gated until every part is present and the native ordered commitment verifies, and conflicting restart retries are rejected. Where an existing local state is independently verified at the exact covered checkpoint, an additional bounded stream comparison now rejects any semantic difference; no match is inferred when the checkpoint differs or is absent. Room v10→11 now stores compact snapshot author heads and unresolved author_gap ranges separately rather than fabricating record IDs; suffix author-chain checks compare the first post-snapshot predecessor against the retained head hash and continue to report snapshot gaps. Chain erasure clears both tables. Focused suffix/equivocation/gap-retention and migration tests pass. The verified-state producer/publication path remains as previously described; no pruning is triggered or authorized, consistent with §7.8/§16.7. A same-log/generation/epoch installation primitive now pages the verified stage into logical Room tables and atomically advances verified/materialized cursor under index-revision CAS; outbox or unresolved quarantine blocks it, and tests cover entity/head/gap install, re-streaming compact author evidence, and splitting a compact gap when a later authenticated record fills it. The existing caller invokes this only after a complete-log replay matches the exact checkpoint and state, so it does not accelerate bootstrap. Snapshot-only source trust and UI, suffix-only continuation from covered_through_seq, handoff and separately authorized pruning remain unimplemented. Still required: isolated-relay and independent-client execution; cancellation, unknown outcome, concurrent log advance and restart fault tests; explicit trusted-source bootstrap/handoff and separately authorized pruning. Full IT-01–IT-50 / Appendix C-D conformance and Android instrumentation remain incomplete.

checklist.requirement: Advertise/request-limit/durability/quota accurately, commit before accepted receipts, preserve sequences/incarnations, reconcile deletion ledger on restore, support bounded export/repair/re-seed.
checklist.remaining: Android can now request device-authorized GET C/export pages with signed cursor query and include_recovery=false, stream the bounded JCS JSONL chunks into a SAF-selected archive, and emit a local hash footer. Device exports correctly remain incomplete for recovery. Still verify relay/export signatures and every object/AEAD before restore, implement receipt-preserving repair and complete generation+1 re-seed/import UI, and exercise crash/ledger/nonce/storage/production boundaries.

checklist.requirement: Reserve 410 for authorized chain deletion and verify deletion proof before local erasure. Treat shutdown/migration/404/outages as recoverable lifecycle states.
checklist.remaining: Authorized CAS request, signed GET /deletion verification, retained proof, explicit SAF readback/offline-copy confirmation, local erase and recovery-material cleanup are implemented. Complete relay-backed CAS/unknown-outcome/410 tests, recovery deletion-guard tests and physical SAF/device verification; keep pending.

checklist.requirement: Publish fully populated operator privacy.md and signed schema-valid privacy.json before use; enforce per-origin/key/body-hash affirmative local consent, current-document revalidation, change/withdrawal pause and no upload of consent records. Show fixed bounds versus configurable quota/tier/key/cache/setup choices.
checklist.remaining: Execute all Android consent/publication-race/change/withdrawal/failure cases and verify production operating facts.

checklist.requirement: Require explicit initial recovery source selection when no known pin/peer exists; keep policy consent separate and never waive cryptographic validation or claim unseen-tail completeness.
checklist.remaining: Test every initial-source UI choice, reject missing ancestry, and show unresolved author/relay completeness separately.

checklist.requirement: Preserve 3.x snapshot/ID limits, retain full required log when complete snapshot cannot fit, and prohibit dependent pruning/key expiry without full state handoff.
checklist.remaining: Exercise maximum part count/external IDs, failed complete-state publication, and dependent pruning/key expiry denial.

checklist.requirement: Implement all catalogue errors and appropriate backoff; never treat an error body as signed authority or discard unsent data on retry.
checklist.remaining: Complete all catalogue operational/quarantine handling and visible capacity/retry-resolution workflows.

checklist.requirement: Validate legacy-to-v3 conversion on frozen input with a resume journal, independent replay comparison and explicit reporting of truncated/corrupt legacy data.
checklist.remaining: Clarify undefined original parameter signature authority; implement verified frozen Android conversion/report/journal/replay.

checklist.requirement: Use vetted compatible GF(256) sharing, fresh RMS/coefficients/RSWKs/nonces, exact canonical input/fingerprint/blob/share AAD and signed bindings; run Appendix C.8.
checklist.remaining: Complete public lifecycle/status propagation, offline issuance/readback/reader UI, and all-valid-threshold independent interoperability.

checklist.requirement: Enforce one persisted piece per physical holder, backup exclusion, separate offline credential, local authentication and live SAS including the separate offline reader. Never send any package/piece/blob to the relay.
checklist.remaining: Complete independent three-party device/offline holder and reader interoperability, live SAS/QR/encrypted-file UI, and OS process/cancel/fault boundaries.

checklist.requirement: Verify all pieces/status/bindings, interpolation/checksum/derived identity before root authorization; explicit setup/ceremony only, no durable secret resume, zeroize on every exit and sanitize audit allowlist.
checklist.remaining: Implement all ceremony UI/authentication/cancellation/failure paths and prove no durable collector shares/RMS/root resume.

checklist.requirement: Display correct `H=t`/`H<t` warnings, compromise/clone/rotation gaps; replace full sets with fresh material and require new root/chain after possible threshold leak.
checklist.remaining: Complete recovery enrollment/full-set rotation/new-root migration and remaining named root operations; validate actual SAF/physical media, public retirement propagation, clone/fault/process-death boundaries and independent three-party ceremonies.

checklist.requirement: Pin relay key to selected origin, atomically sign/persist upload/transparency receipts, keep existing LogEntry hash bytes unchanged and verify complete streaming inclusion links.
checklist.remaining: Execute forged/omitted/conflicting original acceptance and retained-anchor scenarios across three parties.

checklist.requirement: Verify a linear transparency suffix in pages of at most 1,000 entries and bounded §17.8 response bytes, from a retained trusted (transparency_id,index,hash) anchor. Check exact next index, each signature/previous hash and recurrence before atomically persisting the verified page checkpoint. Check cancellation between pages; resume from that checkpoint with the same target/head, retaining unresolved gaps. Keep only a bounded page in RAM, expose verified/target counts and pending status, and never advance over unavailable or unverified entries. Work and transfer are O(unverified suffix); no constant-size Merkle proof is claimed. Data relay_seq and transparency entry_index are independent namespaces.
checklist.remaining: The exact signed target is stored only after its signature and data-head view are checked, then reused across cancellation/restart until the saved verified anchor reaches its entry_index. Each page checks coroutine cancellation before requesting the next page. Focused target-selection tests pass. Run isolated-relay cancellation/process-death at every page boundary and large suffix/post-pruning Android progress tests; keep pending.

checklist.requirement: Export/verify DeletionEvidenceBundle separately from the immutable DeleteReceipt; hash the complete signed receipt and verify each witness's exact binding and authorization-time certified key. Completion revisions need their own bundles.
checklist.remaining: The client preserves distinct signed receipt revisions by object hash, validates monotone completion revisions against the prior retained receipt, and creates each exported bundle against that exact receipt hash. Export restores and persists the union of independently verified local witness bundles for one exact receipt; conflicting signatures for one device ID fail as equivocation. Room tests cover multiple bundle revisions for one receipt, and focused merge tests cover disjoint-device union/order and conflicts. Rust tests verify 128 certified unique witnesses, reject 129 with C_SCHEMA_VIOLATION, reject a bundle reused against a newly signed completion revision, and cover completion monotonicity. The SAF witness export readback and all deletion-evidence archive inputs use the same 256 KiB bound; focused Android archive/merge tests, full Rust tests, detekt and ktlint pass. Still run the full IT-44 negative catalogue, JNI/device archive roundtrip, distinct-device file-exchange instrumentation and physical SAF verification; keep pending.

checklist.requirement: Run bounded consistency probes, retain immutable checkpoint/equivocation evidence, authenticate migrations explicitly and preserve keys on unverified 410.
checklist.remaining: Execute start/resume/unknown/destructive/periodic probes and authenticated relay migration with retained contradiction evidence.

checklist.requirement: Preserve ledger/attestation anti-resurrection evidence through restore, export public deletion evidence and verify optional intent witnesses without making them deletion authority.
checklist.remaining: Execute stale restore/ledger reconciliation, public deletion export, optional witness and anti-resurrection client workflows.

interoperability.scenario: Run all Appendix C JCS positives/negatives in each implementation; reorder received object members/whitespace.
interoperability.expected: Byte/hash match; signatures verify after re-canonicalization; invalid tokens rejected before numeric conversion.

interoperability.scenario: Same 24-word mnemonic/passphrase on two fresh devices; different passphrase as control.
interoperability.expected: Same v3 chain/admin/recovery outputs; independently generated device keys differ; control chain differs.

interoperability.scenario: Encrypt/sign one queryable and one private record, then alter each AAD field/tag/ciphertext.
interoperability.expected: Unchanged fixture applies; tampered signature/AEAD/tag/profile quarantines with appropriate code; no partial record applied.

interoperability.scenario: Use a valid token twice concurrently; retry with fresh token but same record; crash relay after first commit.
interoperability.expected: One nonce consumption; other request TOKEN_REPLAYED; exact record retry returns original receipt, no duplicate operation/sequence.

interoperability.scenario: Replay to another origin/method/path/query/body; test TTL 120/300/301 seconds and ±60-second boundaries.
interoperability.expected: Exact binding and specified freshness acceptance/rejection; implementations issue only 120-second tokens.

interoperability.scenario: Shuffle and duplicate all Appendix D events in all permutations; compare SQLite and in-memory model.
interoperability.expected: Identical winners/order/tombstones/clear/policy registers; duplicate application changes no counters/counts.

interoperability.scenario: Concurrent delete/upsert and clear/upsert at equal Lamport; delayed old event after snapshot.
interoperability.expected: Rank-one suppresses upsert; scoped effects only; tombstone/floor survives bootstrap.

interoperability.scenario: Two favorite inserts into same gap, concurrent moves and 256-digit exhaustion.
interoperability.expected: Rational/lexical order agree, K/entity tie deterministic; exhaustion never silently reindexes.

interoperability.scenario: Upsert one search/viewed entity 10,000 times, reverse/deduplicate replay.
interoperability.expected: One row, greatest K first; no delete-and-recreate or replay-based reorder; seen remains minimal.

interoperability.scenario: Generate ceiling+1 live histories using a small parameterized fixture for fast testing, then one real-size disk stress run per declared supported platform.
interoperability.expected: Default no logical loss/no refused write solely by count; deterministic cold projection; memory independent of total rows within declared worker/page budget.

interoperability.scenario: Turn user stop on, add new entity beyond ceiling, receive a remote excess entry; delete one then retry.
interoperability.expected: Local intent paused, remote valid entry retained, explicit delete frees capacity; no automatic tombstones.

interoperability.scenario: Build multi-part complete snapshot with cold history/deletes/clear/policy/author evidence; change part order/hash/state commitment or omit one old row.
interoperability.expected: Trusted/recomputed original matches full replay; altered/incomplete parts fail; signature alone is not accepted as proof of no semantic omission.

interoperability.scenario: Crash during snapshot download/install and after record apply before cursor save; restart.
interoperability.expected: Staging resumes by hashes; live DB never partially replaced; apply/cursor atomic and idempotent.

interoperability.scenario: Two next-epoch proposals from same head, missing recovery/member envelope, tampered commitment, restart after CAS.
interoperability.expected: Exactly one commit; failures leave head unchanged; all members obtain same secret; checkpoint detects inconsistent branch.

interoperability.scenario: Schedule due while mnemonic unavailable; perform retain/windowed/immediate rotations with and without complete rekey snapshot.
interoperability.expected: Due status without key derivation; expiration postponed until full state handoff; no automatic history loss.

interoperability.scenario: Attempt unsigned enrollment, wrong SAS, subject replacement, certificate key mismatch, pending upload, revoked re-registration.
interoperability.expected: All refused as specified; pending keys ack activates only approved current subject; no unconditional self-heal.

interoperability.scenario: Revoke device, replay an independently pinned pre-revocation record and an unproven backdated old record.
interoperability.expected: Proven history retained; new writes denied; unproven malicious acceptance is marked C_ACCEPTANCE_UNPROVEN, not trusted by clock.

interoperability.scenario: Restore stale backup, keep/change log_id, withhold an author tail, supply conflicting pinned prefix.
interoperability.expected: Declared restore uses new log_id; known prefix mismatch suspends; visible gaps tracked; permanently unseen tail is documented undetectable.

interoperability.scenario: Export in small chunks, interrupt/resume, import/re-seed next generation at target, race old-source write.
interoperability.expected: Archive/footer/source verification succeeds; target state equals verified source prefix; new audience/generation required; raced suffix reported.

interoperability.scenario: Trigger quota/rate/storage failures; repeat accepted upload after uncertain network response.
interoperability.expected: Capacity errors preserve outbox; Retry-After/backoff obeyed; no record-ID mutation for exact retry.

interoperability.scenario: Emit unconfirmed encrypted deletion notice/HTML 410; then authorized ledger deletion; restore an old backup.
interoperability.expected: Unconfirmed signals preserve keys; verified deletion erases local chain; ledger prevents resurrection; upgrades/moves never 410.

interoperability.scenario: Convert `/1` arrays and `/2` granular events, NFC collisions, random legacy salt, truncated legacy history; interrupt every upload.
interoperability.expected: Correct /3 identities/order/signatures, resumable exact journal, no fabricated missing history/authority, explicit collision/loss report.

interoperability.scenario: Prune an approved snapshot prefix, replay removed ID with same/different content, validate suffix hash from boundary.
interoperability.expected: Same covered ID no-op; conflicting ID quarantined; exact state and hash continuity preserved; required verification history survives.

interoperability.scenario: Feed valid unsupported collection, malformed record, missing key, counter exhaustion and history-index revision during paging.
interoperability.expected: Distinct unsupported/quarantine/dependency/operational handling; no global destructive recovery; page cursor either stays pinned or explicitly restarts.

interoperability.scenario: Generate 2-of-3, 2-of-4, 3-of-4 and 3-of-5 under independent GF libraries; test every threshold subset and shuffled duplicate messages.
interoperability.expected: Same RMS/input/chain identity; n−t losses tolerated; same piece counts once.

interoperability.scenario: Reject `t=1,n=t,n<t,n>255`, repeated holder/index and a second device package across chains.
interoperability.expected: Setup/refill refused with specified local code; no secret second persistent slot.

interoperability.scenario: Lose one of a 2-of-3 set, then a second; lose offline credential instead of medium.
interoperability.expected: H=2 next-loss warning, H=1 already unavailable; no automatic ceremony or fabricated missing piece.

interoperability.scenario: Leak one piece/blob, regenerate full set; mix old/new indexes; retain t old pieces/blob as adversary.
interoperability.expected: Mixed sets rejected; new material differs; retained old threshold still recovers old root and is reported as the fundamental limit.

interoperability.scenario: Supply wrong set/blob/AAD/commitment/status branch/fingerprint/passphrase and insufficient pieces.
interoperability.expected: No privileged operation/root session before all checks; distinct safe codes; valid packages survive.

interoperability.scenario: Offline encrypted QR/file roundtrip with separate credential, trusted reader and collector; wrong/missing SAS, stale session and packet replay.
interoperability.expected: Both live confirmations required; ciphertext replay idempotent; no piece leaves endpoint before approval; direct passive scan alone refused.

interoperability.scenario: Interrupt setup/rotation/ceremony at each transition; inspect DB, backup, temp files, crash output and audits.
interoperability.expected: No root/RMS/raw shares/secret blob copies leak; correct prepared/incomplete status; RAM-only recollection after crash; one persisted piece.

interoperability.scenario: Compromise holder/OS backup, revoke device, replace DeviceRecord, enroll new device and change BIP39 passphrase.
interoperability.expected: Revocation does not revoke copies; no auto-share allocation; full-set replacement; passphrase/root change creates new chain; threshold leak cannot be cured same-root.

interoperability.scenario: Upload a multi-entry transaction, exact retry and restart between commit/response; alter receipt signature/hash/link/index.
interoperability.expected: One immutable receipt per log object, original retry receipts, atomic attestation commit; invalid receipt suspends without losing outbox.

interoperability.scenario: Stream transparency suffix from pinned anchor with small pages; fork/rollback/hide tail, withhold intermediate proof and forge new relay key.
interoperability.expected: Correct hashes/heads; contradiction quarantines; missing proof pending; isolated unseen tail undetectable; key replacement never automatic.

interoperability.scenario: Send malicious migration notice/redirect to new origin, valid TLS with conflicting chain/admin/epoch/registry pins.
interoperability.expected: No automatic token/data transfer or erasure; explicit origin selection and full continuity required; aud matches actual selected origin.

interoperability.scenario: Probe concurrently advancing heads, unexplained min_available_seq, own accepted record withholding, unverified 410 and signed contradictory deletion.
interoperability.expected: Concurrent cuts reconciled; gaps reported; positive contradictions suspend writes/destructive actions and preserve keys/evidence.

interoperability.scenario: Verify admin/device deletion with optional distinct active intent witnesses; missing authority, duplicate/invalid witness, stale backup resurrection.
interoperability.expected: Witnesses never replace authority/physical erasure; unverified deletion keeps keys; valid ledger blocks restore and public evidence export is offered.

interoperability.scenario: Complete/cancel/resume bounded attestation export, restore lost suffix with new IDs and compare source/target receipts after re-seed.
interoperability.expected: Exact pinned cuts/footer/proof links; old evidence preserved; target receipts do not impersonate source; no federation or secret recovery artifact export.

interoperability.scenario: Missing/incomplete operator policy, wrong-origin redirect, HTML/invalid UTF-8/oversized body, anonymous fetch and same-origin valid 304.
interoperability.expected: Deployment discloses actual choices; no chain token/ID/data before valid affirmative consent; failed refresh pauses even with an old cache.

interoperability.scenario: No answer, preselection, timeout, reject/withdraw, altered policy body with unchanged revision, new origin/key and client restart.
interoperability.expected: No automatic consent; exact binding/current hash required; keys/outbox/local export retained; key trust/source selection remain independent.

interoperability.scenario: First recovery without pin/known peer; accept policy but omit source choice; explicitly select valid/forged/conflicting source.
interoperability.expected: Separate source guard; valid selected input fully checked, invalid crypto/pins never overridden, isolated completeness limit displayed.

interoperability.scenario: Validate 65,536 versus 65,537 snapshot parts, 2^53−1 versus 2^53 numeric ID bodies, ext/schema/policy attempts to raise limits.
interoperability.expected: In-range formats retain existing validation; out-of-range rejected, full log retained, no incomplete-snapshot pruning, no 3.x exception or rounded/string-substituted /3 body.

interoperability.scenario: Mandatory Shamir implementation with no set, supported UI t/n subset and restoration of valid other profile configuration; small local cache; lower relay quotas/tier/manual key replacement.
interoperability.expected: Capability implemented with explicit not_provisioned setup; valid profile restoration supported, archive/projection/cache distinguished, truthful disclosures/consent and independent key trust required.

interoperability.scenario: Original DeleteReceipt plus 0/1/128 witnesses, duplicate IDs, wrong receipt hash and completion revision.
interoperability.expected: Immutable receipt has no witness member; separate bundle verifies exact original hash, unique certified witnesses; prior bundle cannot attest a new receipt revision.

interoperability.scenario: Complete snapshot divided across different legal part boundaries and with one cold/tombstone/author-gap entry omitted.
interoperability.expected: Same canonical full stream produces identical existing record_key HMAC; omitted state or epoch/generation mismatch is rejected.

interoperability.scenario: Scope count at MAX_* and MAX_*+1 with default policy, then explicit stop preference and physical/quota exhaustion.
interoperability.expected: Default writes and remote apply continue in cold storage; only explicit local stop or actual capacity pauses; snapshots include full cold state and pruning needs handoff.

interoperability.scenario: Signed disclosure missing a required field, altered Markdown, invalid signature, impossible backup tier, regressed revision, health/quota mismatch and valid changed pair.
interoperability.expected: Invalid pair pauses; no chain token/data sent before explicit consent; changed valid pair requires new bound consent; truth of physical erasure is not asserted.

interoperability.scenario: Client TTL120s; server token TTL300s/300s+1ms; restart issued times B−1/B and repeated restart.
interoperability.expected: Client authors120s; server ceiling300s inclusive; B−1 rejected/B eligible under other checks; fresh retry and visible coordinated recovery wait, never enrollment/erasure.

interoperability.scenario: 1,024 small operations, fewer oversized operations, one operation exceeding frame capacity, request encoding overflow.
interoperability.expected: Count and exact byte preflight independently enforced; legal batches split with new IDs, single oversized operation gives C_LOCAL_LIMIT, request overflow PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.

interoperability.scenario: Linear transparency suffix across multiple pages, cancellation/restart and missing page.
interoperability.expected: Atomic verified page anchor resumes; bounded memory, strict signatures/links/indexes, no advancement across missing proof and visible O(suffix) progress.
